angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 636,927 km at 157.86 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.3347 +/- 0.0124 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 157.86 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.915519 solar radii from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-799 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract): 636,927 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.999 (0.959 to 1.039) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5662.81 K from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-799 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-799 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-799.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.514, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
